name: Totemist
body:
Totemists act as the medicine men and specialist warriors of their people. Through precise dance and chanting, a single totemist can whip his allies into frenzy or protect them from a cascade of fire.

Totemists recognize that, though rare, magic does still exist on the continent of Pnumadesi. They harness some of that power to aid themselves and others during combat. The threat of the elementals provides totemists plenty of reason to continue perfecting their use of this magic in the hopes that, eventually, they can pull off more complicated tricks quickly.

Role: Totemists blur the line between combatant and healer. Their resonance is one way to help better define which role they follow. A totemist may choose to focus on weapons, implements, or healing, and the choice they make builds on their talents.

Alignment: Any neutral.

Hit Die: d8.

Parent Classes: Bard and druid.

Class Skills: The totemist’s class skills are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (all) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are class features of the totemist.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Totemists are proficient with the following weapons: club, dagger, dart, quarterstaff, scimitar, scythe, sickle, shortspear, sling, and spear.

Totemists are proficient with light and medium armor but are prohibited from wearing metal armor; thus, they may wear only padded, leather, or hide armor. A totemist may also wear wooden armor that has been altered by the ironwood spell so that it functions as though it were steel. Totemists are proficient with shields (except tower shields) but must use only wooden ones.

A totemist who wears prohibited armor or uses a prohibited shield is unable to cast totemist spells or use any of his supernatural or spell-like class abilities while doing so and for 24 hours thereafter.

Spellcasting

A totemist casts divine spells drawn from the totemist spell list. He can cast any spell he knows without preparing it ahead of time. Every totemist spell has a somatic component (such as dancing or rhythmic movement and chanting).

At 1st level, choose Wisdom or Charisma as the totemist’s spellcasting ability score. Once this choice is made, it can’t be changed. To learn or cast a spell, a totemist must have a spellcasting ability score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class (DC) for a saving throw against a totemist’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the totemist’s spellcasting ability modifier

Like other spellcasters, a totemist can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. His base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Totemist. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if he has a high spellcasting ability score.

The totemist’s selection of spells is extremely limited. A totemist begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of the totemist’s choice. At each new totemist level, he gains one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: Totemist Spells Known. (Unlike spells per day, the number of spells a totemist knows is not affected by his spellcasting ability score.

Upon reaching 5th level, and at every third totemist level after that (8th, 11th, and so on), a totemist can choose to learn a new spell in place of one he already knows. In effect, the totemist “loses” the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged, and it must be at least one level lower than the highest-level totemist spell the totemist can cast. A totemist may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that he gains new spells known for the level.

A totemist need not prepare his spells in advance. He can cast any spell he knows at any time, assuming he has not yet used up his allotment of spells per day for the spell’s level.

Orisons: Totemist’s learn a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, as noted on Table: Totemist Spells Known under “Spells Known.” These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again.

Nature’s Bond (Ex)

At 1st level, a totemist forms a bond with nature. This bond can take one of three forms: Animal companion, druidic herbalism, and totemist domain. once this choice is made, it can’t be changed.

Animal Companion

The totemist begins play with any of the animals available to a druid. This animal is a loyal companion that accompanies the totemist on his adventures.

Unlike normal animals of its kind, an animal companion’s Hit Dice, abilities, skills, and feats advance as the totemist advances in level. If the totemist receives an animal companion from more than one source, his effective totemist levels stack for the purposes of determining the statistics and abilities of the companion.

Most animal companions increase in size when their totemist reaches 4th or 7th level, depending on the companion. If a totemist releases his companion from service, he may gain a new one by performing a ceremony requiring 24 uninterrupted hours of prayer in the environment where the new companion typically lives. This ceremony can also replace an animal companion that has perished.

Druidic Herbalism

A totemist who chooses to learn druidic herbalism can use combinations of nuts, berries, dried herbs, and other natural ingredients along with appropriate containers to create herbal concoctions or magic consumables that function like potions. This acts like the Brew Potion feat, but only for spells on the totemist spell list. Herbal concoctions created with herbs that cause special effects when ingested retain those effects as well as the appropriate spell effect.

A totemist can create a number of free herbal concoctions per day equal to his Wisdom modifier. Additional concoctions cost the same as creating an equivalent potion using Brew Potion. Druids can sell their herbal concoctions just as if they were potions.

At 4th level, a totemist’s increasing skill with herbalism means that he can disguise the effects of his herbal concoctions. When a creature attempts a Perception or Spellcraft check to identify one of the totemist’s concoctions, the concoction appears to be a different herbal concoction of the totemist’s choice unless the creature exceeds the identification DC by 5 or more. The totemist must designate this false result when creating the concoction. If a creature exceeds the identification DC by 5 or more, it correctly identifies the concoction, though not that the totemist tried to fool it.

Additionally, at 4th level, when the totemist creates additional concoctions, he need pay only half the normal cost to create them.

It takes him only half the normal time to create his concoctions, and he can create concoctions of spells from any spell list, as long as he can cast the spell.

At 7th level, when the totemist creates concoctions with potential false identification results, a creature attempting to identify the concoction must exceed the identification DC by 10 or more to determine the concoction’s true identity.

Additionally, at 7th level, a totemist can create any herbal concoction in 1 minute. He can also create a special concoction of any spell higher than 3rd level that he can cast, but to do so, he must expend a spell slot of the same level. These special concoctions do not cost him anything to create and function like extracts created by an alchemist with the infusion discovery.

Totemist Domain: The totemist forms a strong bond to the ideas of family, nature, and the spiritual world, which grants him one of the following cleric domains or subdomains. He also has access to the druid’s Animal and Terrain Domains.

Air, Ancestors, Animal, Community, Earth, Exploration, Fate, Fire, Glory, Healing, Lust, Moon, Music, Plant, Revelry, Rites, Rune, Strength, Water, or Weather

When determining the powers and bonus spells granted by this domain, the totemist’s effective cleric level is equal to his totemist level. A totemist that selects this option can cast each of his domain spells once per day without spending a spell slot, and he can’t use his spell slots to cast those spells unless they are also on the totemist spell list.

Resonance (Su)

Resonance is the practice of feeling magic as it vibrates through reality when being cast, and manipulating those vibrations for unexpected outcomes. A totemist use this ability a number of times per day equal to 4 + his spellcasting ability modifier. At each level after 1st a totemist can use resonance 2 additional times per day. When Table: Totemist lists resonance, the totemist can learn one resonance effect for which he meets the prerequisites and requirements, if any. A full list of resonance effects can be found at the end of this section. As he gains experience, the totemist also learns three special resonance chants (ancestral, bold, and heroic), which are detailed below.

When he casts a totemist spell, the totemist can add resonance to it by spending an amount of resonance described by the effect.

If a resonance effect needs to be maintained, the totemist can maintain it as a free action on his turn. A maintained resonance cannot be disrupted, but it ends immediately if the totemist is killed, paralyzed, stunned, knocked unconscious, or otherwise prevented from taking a free action to maintain it each round. A totemist cannot maintain more than one resonance at one time.

Each resonance adds audible components, visual components, or both to the spell it modifies.

If a resonance has audible components, the targets must be able to hear the totemist for the modified spell to have any effect, and such resonance effects may be language dependent (as noted in the description). A deaf totemist has a 20% chance to fail when attempting to use a resonance with an audible component. If he fails this check, the attempt still counts against his total, but does not expend the spell slot. Deaf creatures are immune to resonance effects with audible components.

If a resonance has a visual component, the targets must have line of sight to the totemist for the spell to have any effect. A blind totemist has a 50% chance to fail when attempting to use a resonance with a visual component. If he fails this check, the attempt still counts against his total, but does not expend the spell slot. Blind creatures are immune to resonance effects with visual components.

Bold Chant (Su)

Audible and Visual

As a standard action, a totemist can spend 1 resonance and begin a bold, rhythmic chant to his ancestors that heartens allies who can see and hear him. This functions as the bard’s inspire courage, and requires the totemist to spend 1 resonance each round to maintain it.

If the totemist is maintaining battle resonance, using bold chant is a move action at 1st level, a swift action at 7th level, and as part of the same action at 13th level. Battle resonance ends, but the totemist retains his battle resonance bonuses if they’re higher than the bonus provided by bold chant.

Spellstrike (Su)

At 2nd level, whenever a totemist casts a spell with a range of “touch” from the totemist spell list, he can deliver the spell through any weapon he is wielding as part of a melee attack.

Instead of the free melee touch attack normally allowed to deliver the spell, a totemist can make one free melee attack with his weapon (at his highest base attack bonus) as part of casting this spell. If successful, this melee attack deals its normal damage as well as the effects of the spell. If the totemist makes this attack in concert with spell combat, this melee attack takes all the penalties accrued by spell combat melee attacks. This attack uses the weapon’s critical range (20, 19–20, or 18–20 and modified by the keen weapon property or similar effects), but the spell effect only deals x2 damage on a successful critical hit, while the weapon damage uses its own critical modifier.

Venom Resistance (Ex)

At 5th level, a totemist gains a +2 bonus on all saving throws against poison. This bonus increases to +4 at 8th level, and then again to +6 at 11th level.

Ancestral Chant (Su)

Audible and Visual

At 12th level, a totemist can spend 9 resonance as a standard action and call upon his ancestors to possess him or one of his willing allies who can see and hear him. This grants the target the effects of transformation while the totemist maintains the resonance, and requires the totemist to spend 1 resonance each round to maintain it.

At 14th level, the totemist can use and maintain ancestral chant on up to two creatures at a time, spending all necessary resonance to do so. At 18th level, he can maintain ancestral chant on up to three total creatures at a time.

If he knows transformation as a totemist spell, this chant costs 6 resonance to use instead.

Guardian’s Chant (Su)

Audible and Visual

At 15th level, a totemist can spend 4 resonance as a standard action—or 6 resonance as an immediate action—to grant himself or an ally within 30 feet who can see and hear him a +4 morale bonus on saving throws and a +4 dodge bonus to AC. The totemist can then maintain this resonance on each of his turns by spending 1 resonance.

At 18th level, the totemist can maintain this resonance on up to two different creatures at a time for no additional cost. He must still use the resonance on a second creature before he can maintain the effect on it.

Greater Spell Access (Ex)

At 19th level, a totemist gains access to an expanded spell list. He learns 14 spells from the bard or druid’s spell as totemist spells of their bard or druid level (whichever is lower). He gains two each of 0- through 6th-level spells.

Grand Totemist (Ex)

At 20th level, a totemist has become a master of resonance, able to harmonize with it on a level unknown to any other. Choose enclave leader, harmonious bond, or true resonance. Once this choice is made, it can only be retrained by spending one month of downtime and 200 gp per totemist level (minimum 4,000 gp).

Enclave Leader: The totemist founds an enclave where he can teach others his ways. He learns druidic and gains the timeless body and tongue of sun and moon monk class features.

Harmonious Bond: The totemist gains a second nature’s bond option. He can choose the totemist domain bond a second time. If he chooses animal companion a second time, his companion gains both the advanced and giant templates.

True Resonance

The totemist gains 3 item creation or metamagic feats for which he meets the prerequisites.

Resonance Effects Animal Resonance Visual

Drawing a representation in the air, you cast the spell and spend 2 resonance to create an animal-themed totem the size of a tiny creature in your empty hand or, if your hands are full, in your space. Once created, creatures can pick up and move the totem. It has hit points equal to your spellcasting ability score and hardness equal to twice your totemist level. You can have one totem at one time. If you create a new totem, your oldest totem fades from existence. You can maintain up to two totems at one time at 6th level, three at 12th level, and four at 18th level. You must still create each totem separately.

When you create the totem, choose an animal from the list here. The totem grants you and allies the benefits associated with that animal as long as you maintain the resonance for no additional cost, up to 1 minute.

Bat: The totem grants blindsense in a 30-foot radius, but costs 1 additional resonance to maintain each round.
Bear: The totem grants a +4 size bonus on grapple combat maneuver checks and to CMD against grapple.
Bison: The totem allows creatures within 30 feet to charge after moving only 5 feet.
Boar: The totem grants temporary hit points equal to your totemist level (minimum 3) to creatures within 30 feet. A creature can only gain these temporary hit points once per use.
Cat: The totem grants a competence bonus on Stealth checks equal to 1/3 your totemist level (minimum 1).
Centipede: The totem grants a +5-foot enhancement bonus to movement speed. This effect stacks with itself.
Crocodile: The totem grants a +2 enhancement bonus to natural armor. This effect stacks with itself twice.
Deer: The totem grants a +1 bonus to initiative checks. This effect stacks with itself, and with similar effects (such as Improved Initiative), up to a total +8 bonus.
Dog: The totem grants scent in a 30-foot radius.
Eagle: The totem grants a competence bonus on Perception checks to see equal to 1/2 your totemist level (minimum 1).
Fox: You gain a bonus to your Charisma ability score equal to your totemic nature bonus.
Hare: The totem grants a competence bonus on Acrobatics checks made to jump equal to 1/2 your totemist level (minimum 1).
Horse: The totem grants +4 Strength for the purpose of determining how much weight can be carried, lifted, pushed, or dragged.
Owl: The totem grants darkvision in a 30-foot radius.
Rat: The totem allows creatures to squeeze through a space as if they were one size-category smaller.
Snake: The totem grants a competence bonus on Diplomacy checks to influence a creature’s attitude equal to 1/2 your totemist level (minimum 1).
Spider: The totem grants creatures the ability to move at half speed while climbing with no penalty, or full speed with a –5 penalty.
Wolf: The totem grants a +4 size bonus on trip combat maneuver checks and to CMD against trip.

Battle Resonance

Audible

With an expressive cry to your warrior ancestors, you cast the spell and spend an amount of resonance up to the difference between your character level and your base attack bonus. You gain a competence bonus to your attacks and weapon damage rolls equal to the resonance spent in this way while you maintain the resonance, up to 1 minute.

Metamagic Resonance

Visual

Prerequisite: 5th level.

As a full-round action, you sweep your arms around to gather power and cast the spell as if you were a sorcerer using exactly one metamagic feat. For every 1 resonance you spend, the spell’s level is increased by 1 less. You must still be able to cast spells of the increased level. For example, if you can cast 2nd-level spells, you can enlarge a 1st-level or lower spell without increasing its spell level by spending 1 resonance. If you don’t know the metamagic feat, this costs 1 additional resonance to use for every 2 resonance you spend (minimum 1).

If a modified spell has a duration greater than instantaneous, you must maintain the resonance on your turn, but it costs no additional resonance to do so.

Spell Resonance

Audible

Prerequisite: 17th level.

With a crack of power centered on you, you cast a totemist spell you know as a 7th-level or higher spell using a lower-level spell slot (to a maximum of 9th). This allows you to apply metamagic resonance to spells you couldn’t normally alter. You apply this resonance, then immediately apply the metamagic resonance as well.

This costs an amount of resonance equal to the difference between the spell slot used and the intended spell level to be cast. This does not grant you those spell slots, so you must still reduce the effective spell level to a slot you can cast.

For example, you can quicken a 5th-level spell by spending 8 total resonance (4 to cast it as a 9th-level spell, and 4 to reduce its spell level since you don’t have 9th-level spell slots), assuming you know the Quicken Spell feat (otherwise, the total cost is 10 resonance).

Favored Class Bonuses
Any: Gain 1/6 of a new resonance effect.
Dwarf: Add +1 to the totemist’s total resonance per day.
Goblin: Deal +1 fire damage with fire spells cast as part of spellstrike.
Human: Add one spell known from the totemist spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest spell level the totemist can cast.
Minotaur: Add +1 to the totemist’s total resonance per day.
Orc: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using battle resonance (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Tiefling: The totemist gains fire resistance 1. Each time this reward is selected, increase fire resistance by +1. This fire resistance does not stack with fire resistance gained from other sources.
Trollkin: Add +1 foot to the size of all totemist’s animal resonance totems. This option has no effect unless the totemist has selected it 5 times (or another increment of 5); a radius of 34 feet is effectively the same as a 30-foot radius, for example.
Ursaren: Gain +1/6 of a new item creation or metamagic feat.
